name: Elbow Escape to Remove Hooks
summary: An Invisible Collar guard reset opens the high leg clinch and restores inside elbows and knees; removing rear hooks belongs to a separate back-control escape.
description: An Invisible Collar guard reset opens the high leg clinch and restores inside elbows and knees; removing rear hooks belongs to a separate back-control escape.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Invisible Collar contains no required rear hooks. Its bottom player controls the facing high guard rather than defending a back mount.

The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

attacker.description: Elbow Escape to Remove Hooks (attacker): The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. Invisible Collar contains no required rear hooks. Its bottom player controls the facing high guard rather than defending a back mount.

The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Bring the forearms and knees between the bodies as space becomes available. Keep the shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent while re-establishing a comfortable facing guard. Check posture, knee comfort and inside space before resuming a sweep or submission attack.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

For the actual Invisible Collar reset, release the high legs and use a small hip escape behind connected elbows and knees. This guard retention protects the space beside the ribs from chest pressure; removing rear hooks would require a different starting configuration.

Restore inside frames: Bring the forearms and knees between the bodies as space becomes available.
Face the opponent: Keep the shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent while re-establishing a comfortable facing guard.
Stabilize before moving again: Check posture, knee comfort and inside space before resuming a sweep or submission attack.

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): Which barrier replaces the opened high clinch?
flashcards.answer: After opening Invisible Collar, restore inside forearms and knees to protect the space the high legs previously controlled.
flashcards.answer_line: Forearms and knees between the two torsos

plausible: Both arms wrapped behind the opponent's head
Both legs extended outside the opponent's hips
trap: Forearms inside with both knees left outside their hips

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What must release before you lower the high legs?
flashcards.answer: Unload the neck and isolated arm before changing the high-leg geometry; lowering the legs must not drag a fixed shoulder.
flashcards.answer_line: Any loaded neck or trapped-arm connection

plausible: Only the second leg, leaving arm torque applied
Only your hand grip, leaving the neck cinched
trap: Only the ankle crossing while the overhook stays loaded

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): How should the raised knee come down?
flashcards.answer: Use hip movement to lower the high leg through free space while keeping the knee comfortable.
flashcards.answer_line: Move the hip so the bent leg lowers comfortably

plausible: Hold the knee still and pull the ankle outward
Straighten the leg against the opponent's shoulder
trap: Flatten the hip first while the foot stays held high

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): Where does the near knee return during recovery?
flashcards.answer: A returning knee closes the torso gap alongside the forearm, helping prevent chest-to-chest access.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside the gap between your ribs and the opponent

plausible: Behind the opponent's head again
Outside the opponent's far hip
trap: Alongside your ribs but outside their approaching arm

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): How should the torso face during this reset?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a facing guard as the high legs lower; turning away exposes space instead of rebuilding the inside barrier.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent

plausible: Shoulders away while the hips face forward
Chest down with both knees behind you
trap: Shoulders facing them with the hips rotated away

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What makes another high-guard entry available?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish posture control and comfortable inside knee space before lifting the leg for another rubber-guard attempt.
flashcards.answer_line: Posture controlled again with knee space restored

plausible: Your ankle touching their shoulder alone
Both hands reaching around an upright head
trap: Knee space restored while their chest stays fully upright

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What should replace the high-leg barrier as you open it?
flashcards.answer: Open your own high clinch and restore forearms and knees between the bodies while you remain facing the opponent. Rear-hook removal would require a separate position behind the torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside forearms and knees in a facing guard

plausible: Both arms reaching behind the opponent's head
Straight legs outside both of the opponent's hips
trap: Inside knees with both forearms held outside their arms

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What would make actual rear-hook removal relevant?
flashcards.answer: Removing rear hooks requires rear torso attachment and actual hooks; facing Invisible Collar does not supply those conditions.
flashcards.answer_line: An opponent attached behind you with hooks inside

plausible: Your second leg closing behind their head
Their free hand framing against your chest
trap: An opponent facing you with feet hooked at your hips

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): Why pair a short hip escape with the inside frame?
flashcards.answer: The forearm maintains the torso gap while a small lateral hip movement creates room for the returning knee.
flashcards.answer_line: The frame holds space while the hips admit a knee

plausible: The frame pulls the opponent over your head
The frame follows their chest as your knee stays outside
trap: The hips move away while both forearms leave the gap

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): Which opening shows the reset still needs work?
flashcards.answer: Chest access through the elbow-knee gap means the inside barrier is incomplete even if the high legs are already down.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's chest entering your elbow-knee gap

plausible: Your near knee meeting your forearm
Your shoulders turning to face the opponent
trap: Their chest stopped outside your connected elbow and knee

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What should precede a turn if their shoulder stays caught?
flashcards.answer: Open the arm connection before rotating the bodies so the captured shoulder can move rather than take the twisting force.
flashcards.answer_line: Release the arm trap before rotating farther

plausible: Pull the wrist farther across your body
Keep the arm pinned and lower both knees
trap: Relax the leg squeeze but keep the loaded overhook

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (bottom): What confirms facing guard has been restored?
flashcards.answer: The completed reset is judged by the recovered inside barrier and facing orientation, not by merely uncrossing the high legs.
flashcards.answer_line: Knees and forearms block access to your torso

plausible: Your second leg has opened but both knees trail
Your hands are free but your chest is pinned
trap: Inside knees while both forearms remain outside their arms

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (top): What does their second leg behind your head add?
flashcards.answer: The free leg closing high reinforces the leg-and-arm enclosure around your upper body, even without jacket grips.
flashcards.answer_line: Reinforcement of the existing high posture clinch

plausible: Restraint of the hips with the head still free
Isolation of both elbows inside a high leg triangle
trap: Release of the first leg's head control

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (top): How should the captured elbow stay while you wait for slack?
flashcards.answer: Keep the caught elbow compact and avoid twisting the torso away while the high enclosure remains attached.
flashcards.answer_line: Near your ribs with the head and shoulder aligned

plausible: Flared away from the body to make a larger loop
Reaching behind the opponent's back
trap: Near your ribs while your chest turns away from it

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (top): How should you relieve a stack as their legs open?
flashcards.answer: Unload the forward pressure that folds the partner onto the neck before continuing the high-guard release.
flashcards.answer_line: Shift weight back off their neck before proceeding

plausible: Lift their hips farther before freeing your head
Widen your knees but keep driving their hips forward
trap: Keep the hips elevated while pulling your head backward

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (top): Where should slack develop before head extraction?
flashcards.answer: Use early frames and balanced positioning to open the high-leg connection before trying to pull your head free.
flashcards.answer_line: At the high leg's hip-and-thigh connection

plausible: At the supporting hand while the high thigh stays tight
Between your own knees while the high leg stays closed
trap: At the free leg while the controlling thigh stays clamped

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar elbow reset (top): Where should the freed elbow return?
flashcards.answer: Once the high closure opens, bring the elbow back inside so it can act as a frame rather than remain isolated.
flashcards.answer_line: Between the bodies beside your ribs

plausible: Onto the mat outside their hip again
Behind their neck with the elbow flared
trap: Along their outer ribs with the hand back inside
